# corpus -- licensed C sources + reproducible ELF corpus

**Source under test** (`UNDER-TEST.md`): the upstream trees, their generated files and the ELF outputs are third-party software kept verbatim to be checked, not part of silmaril-lean.

Pinned upstream C sources (verbatim, with their licence texts), a reproducible build for **x86_64**
(native gcc) and **aarch64** (Debian cross gcc) in one pinned toolchain image, and the resulting ELF
files under `corpus/elf/`. Every ELF is **not stripped** (`.symtab` kept: a later step proves
function decompositions from the symbol table) and has **no debug info** (`-g0`, no `.debug_*`
sections; `has_debug_info: false` in every receipt), is built at `-O2` with
`-ffile-prefix-map=/build/<pkg>=.` and a fixed `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, and was built twice from clean
with byte-identical results.

## Contract (layout)

```
corpus/README.md                 this file; the object table below is rewritten by mktable.py
corpus/toolchain/{Dockerfile,lock.txt,image.sh}
corpus/build-all.sh              builds every package for both arches in the image; --check compares with
                                         the committed SHA256SUMS; --collect also refreshes upstream/ + generated/
corpus/common.sh                 (ours) helper sourced by every build.sh / test.sh inside the image
corpus/fetch-lib.sh              (ours) helper sourced by every fetch.sh (host side)
corpus/depfiles.py               (ours) lists the files named by compiler depfiles (*.d, .deps/*.Po)
corpus/receipt.py                (ours) measures the outputs and writes receipt.json + SHA256SUMS
corpus/mktable.py                (ours) regenerates the table below from the receipts
corpus/<pkg>/package.toml        name, version, category, summary, SPDX licence, licence files, [[archive]], [[object]]
corpus/<pkg>/upstream/<root>/... verbatim upstream files only: the subset the build read (depfiles) + licence/attribution files
corpus/<pkg>/upstream.sha256     sha256sum of every file under upstream/ (relative paths)
corpus/<pkg>/generated/<arch>/   configure/build-generated sources the compiler read (marked by GENERATED.txt)
corpus/<pkg>/local/              repository-authored files (drivers, patches, shims, helpers), each with a header saying why
corpus/<pkg>/fetch.sh            downloads the upstream archive(s) into $CORPUS_CACHE and checks sha256
corpus/<pkg>/build.sh            `build.sh ARCH OUTDIR`, runs INSIDE the image, fetches nothing: verifies the cached
                                         archive sha256, extracts, configures, builds, copies the objects to OUTDIR
corpus/<pkg>/test.sh             `test.sh ARCH OBJDIR`, runs inside the image: x86_64 natively, aarch64 under
                                         qemu-user (`qemu-aarch64 -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu`); results go to receipt.json
corpus/elf/<pkg>/<arch>/<object>   the ELF outputs (arch: x86_64, aarch64)
corpus/elf/<pkg>/<arch>/receipt.json
corpus/elf/<pkg>/<arch>/SHA256SUMS
corpus/twin.sh, funcmap.py       (ours) debug twins (-g instead of -g0; .text and function symbols checked identical
                                         to the pinned object) and the function -> C source map they give
corpus/<pkg>/funcmap/<arch>/<object>.json   that map (tool-derived)
corpus/tv.py                     (ours) per-function translation-validation contexts and blockers
corpus/<pkg>/tv/<arch>/<object>.tsv         the contexts (one line per function); corpus/TV.md: the coverage matrix
corpus/DECOMP.md                 the structural decompositions (generated by scripts/corpus/gen.py)
Silmaril/Elf/Staged/Corpus/<Pkg>/<Arch>/<Obj>/{Bytes,Defs,Thms,Functions,Decomp}.lean   kernel-checked parts,
                                         function symbols and structural decompositions of each object (scripts/corpus/gen.py)
```

`receipt.json` fields: `package, version, arch, image {tag, id, base}, compiler` (`gcc --version`
first line), `binutils` (`ld --version` first line), `cflags, ldflags, configure_args,
build_commands` (representative compile/link lines taken from the build log), `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH,
build_dir, inputs [{url, sha256}], outputs [{object, path, size, sha256, elf_machine, func_symbols,
has_symtab, has_debug_info}], reproducible, tests [{command, result}]`, and `notes` where relevant.
`func_symbols` = number of `.symtab` entries of type FUNC with nonzero size and a defined section
(`readelf -sW`, Ndx != UND). Every number is measured on the built file by `receipt.py`.

`package.toml` follows this schema (`name, version, category, summary, license` (SPDX),
`license_files, homepage, [[archive]] {url, sha256, root, retrieved}, [[object]] {name, kind,
sources | sources_list, cflags, notes}`); some archives carry extra `notes` / signature fields.

## How to rebuild / check

```sh
corpus/toolchain/image.sh                 # builds silmaril-corpus-toolchain:trixie-20251103, prints the image id
CORPUS_CACHE=~/.cache/silmaril-corpus corpus/build-all.sh            # all packages, both arches -> corpus/elf
CORPUS_CACHE=~/.cache/silmaril-corpus corpus/build-all.sh --check    # rebuild in a temp dir, compare with SHA256SUMS
corpus/build-all.sh --collect sqlite      # maintainer: also refresh sqlite/upstream, upstream.sha256, generated/
```
Docker on our hosts has no bridge network, so every `docker build` / `docker run` uses `--network host`.
Check that upstream/ is verbatim: unpack the archive and run `sha256sum -c upstream.sha256` from the
directory that contains the archive root (for refcrypto, unpack all seven inputs side by side, the
zip into `rijndael-fst-3.0/` and `rfc6234.txt` into `rfc6234/`).

## Toolchain (one pinned image for everything)

* `toolchain/Dockerfile`: `FROM debian:trixie-20251103@sha256:01a723bf5bfb21b9dda0c9a33e0538106e4d02cce8f557e118dd61259553d598`,
  apt sources = `snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian/20251103T000000Z` (trixie, trixie-updates) and
  `.../debian-security/20251103T000000Z` with `Check-Valid-Until false`. The snapshot was reachable
  and used (no fallback to deb.debian.org). It is addressed over **http** (the base image has no CA
  certificates before ca-certificates is installed; apt verifies the Release files with the Debian
  archive keys, so integrity does not depend on TLS). Exact versions of all 210 installed packages:
  `toolchain/lock.txt` (`dpkg-query -W`).
* Image id (built 2026-11-17): `sha256:42e6f05098b3fd5e3439f33b0ce83fa8601b0af0829d59f22b754b98fed690c2`
  (tag `silmaril-corpus-toolchain:trixie-20251103`).
* x86_64: gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, GNU ld 2.44 (binutils 2.44-3), glibc 2.41-12.
  aarch64: aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0 (gcc-14-aarch64-linux-gnu 14.2.0-19cross1),
  binutils-aarch64-linux-gnu 2.44-3, libc6-dev-arm64-cross 2.41-11cross1.
  qemu-user 1:10.0.3+ds-0+deb13u1 (`qemu-aarch64 -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu`). make 4.4.1, perl 5.40.1, python3 3.13.5.

## Build conventions (all packages)

* Fixed build directory `/build/<pkg>` inside a fresh container; `-ffile-prefix-map=/build/<pkg>=.`;
  `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1762128000` (2025-11-03T00:00:00Z, the image date); `LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC umask 022`.
* Base flags `-O2 -g0 -ffile-prefix-map=/build/<pkg>=.`; package build systems add their own flags
  (recorded per receipt). Debian gcc defaults apply (PIE executables; no other hardening flags).
  Where a package's own build does not write depfiles, `-MMD` is added; it only writes a `.d` file.
* No stripping anywhere; no install step.
* Reproducibility: `build-all.sh` builds each (package, arch) twice in two fresh containers and
  compares the sha256 of every object; all 20 (package, arch) pairs were byte-identical
  (`reproducible: true`), and `build-all.sh --check` reproduced every committed SHA256SUMS.

Per-package notes:

* **sqlite** -- 3.54.1, the latest release (archive SHA3-256 checked against sqlite.org's download page). The amalgamation is compiled directly (`-DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1`,
  otherwise default options). `sqlite3ext.h` is not read by this build, so it is not in upstream/.
  The licence is the blessing in each file header; `local/COPYRIGHT-sqlite.txt` adds a verbatim excerpt
  of https://sqlite.org/copyright.html.
* **cjson** -- Uses upstream's CMake default flags, written out as gcc commands. `libcjson_utils.so.1` links
  against `libcjson.so.1` (as CMake does). Upstream's plain Makefile would copy cJSON.o into it instead.
* **jemalloc** -- Built with the shipped configure and make. To avoid build-host detection we pass
  `--with-lg-page=12` (x86_64), `--with-lg-page=16` (aarch64, as Debian's arm64 package does) and
  `--with-lg-hugepage=21`. configure's own `-O3 -funroll-loops -g3` come first on each compile line,
  so our later `-O2 -g0` wins. `-funroll-loops` stays in effect.
* **mimalloc** -- No CMake in the image: the commands are those of its CMakeLists for Linux/gcc with
  default options, and `-O2 -DNDEBUG` instead of Release's `-O3 -DNDEBUG`. On aarch64 we add
  `-march=armv8.1-a` because upstream's MI_OPT_ARCH=ON default does.
* **darkhttpd** -- Built with upstream's Makefile.
* **tcp-pingpong** -- `upstream/` holds Beej's `server.c` and `client.c` verbatim from the pinned git
  commit. The beej.us website copies differ slightly; see `local/LICENSE-NOTE.txt`. `local/pingpong.patch`
  is ours ("adapted from Beej's Guide"): the client sends "ping", the server answers "pong", for N rounds.
  The public-domain grant is quoted in `local/LICENSE-NOTE.txt`.
* **refcrypto** -- One library per family. All inputs are pinned and listed in `refcrypto/package.toml`:
  * SHA-1/SHA-2, HMAC and HKDF: the RFC 6234 text. The C files are cut out of it by our
    `local/extract-rfc6234.py`, which only removes page headers and footers; the result is in
    `generated/<arch>/rfc6234/`.
  * SHA-3: XKCP `Keccak-readable-and-compact.c`.
  * BLAKE2: BLAKE2 `ref/blake2{b,s}-ref.c`.
  * AES: the original Rijndael fst 3.0 zip, retrieved through the Internet Archive. Two independent
    snapshots have the same sha256.
  * ChaCha20: SUPERCOP `crypto_stream/chacha20/e/ref`, which is DJB's chacha-ref with 20 rounds, the
    original 64-bit nonce layout and the `crypto_stream_chacha20{,_xor}` wrappers.
  * Poly1305: poly1305-donna.
  * Ed25519: orlp/ed25519, a copy of ref10.
  * X25519: SUPERCOP `crypto_scalarmult/curve25519/ref10`.

  SUPERCOP generates `crypto_stream.h` / `crypto_scalarmult.h` at benchmark time; our two stand-ins are
  in `local/supercop-shim/`. `CRYPTO_NAMESPACE` is passed with `-D`, as SUPERCOP does.
  `local/kat.c` is ours and is test-only: 32 known-answer tests from FIPS 180-4, FIPS 197, FIPS 202 and
  RFCs 4231, 5869, 7693, 7748, 8032 and 8439.
* **coreutils** -- Built with the genuine `./configure && make`, cross with `--host=aarch64-linux-gnu`.
  Options: `--disable-nls --without-selinux --without-openssl --without-libgmp --disable-acl
  --disable-xattr --disable-libcap --disable-libsmack --without-systemd --disable-rpath`.
  `FORCE_UNSAFE_CONFIGURE=1` is set because the image builds as root. The build makes `$(BUILT_SOURCES)`
  (listed with our `local/print-var.mk`) and then only `src/{true,echo,cat,wc,head,sort,sha256sum}`.
  The cross configure needed **no** cache variables: gnulib's conservative cross guesses were used, and
  the guessed checks are listed in `generated/<arch>/configure-cross-guesses.txt`. As a result the
  aarch64 build pulls in some gnulib replacement functions that the native build does not. upstream/
  holds the sources of the seven programs and **all** of `lib/` that make compiled into
  `lib/libcoreutils.a` (the archive the programs link against), not only the members the linker kept.
  Tarball signature: `gpgv` reports "Good signature from Pádraig Brady", key 6C37DC12121A5006BC1DB804DF6FD971306037D9,
  checked against https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gnu-keyring.gpg. `fetch.sh` repeats this check when gpgv is available.
* **openssl** -- Configured with `./Configure linux-x86_64 | linux-aarch64 --cross-compile-prefix=aarch64-linux-gnu- no-asm shared no-tests`
  and `CFLAGS='-O2 -g0 -ffile-prefix-map=/build/openssl=.'`, which replaces Configure's default `-O3`.
  **no-asm is deliberate**: every function is C, which the later translation-validation step needs.
  The build runs `make build_libs apps/openssl` only, so the legacy provider and engine modules are not
  built. `crypto/buildinf.h` honours SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Generated headers (`include/openssl/*.h` from
  `.in`), `configdata.pm`, `buildinf.h`, the providers' generated DER sources and `apps/progs.[ch]` are
  in `generated/<arch>/`. The tarball's sha256 equals the published `.sha256` file; no PGP check was done.

* **tinycc** -- `./configure` (`--cpu=aarch64 --cross-prefix=aarch64-linux-gnu- --triplet=aarch64-linux-gnu` for
  aarch64) and `make tcc`. The compiler targets the architecture it runs on. `libtcc1.a`, tcc's runtime
  library compiled by tcc itself, is not built. The test compiles a C program with the built tcc
  (`tcc -c`), links it with gcc (`-no-pie` on aarch64: tcc 0.9.27 emits absolute `R_AARCH64_MOVW_UABS_*`
  relocations) and runs it. Savannah publishes no `.sig` for 0.9.27, so the tarball is pinned by sha256 only.

## What is proved, what is mapped, what is open

* **Proved (kernel, standard axioms)** for every object: each part of the file (`Thms`), each function
  symbol (`Functions`), and per executable section a **structural decomposition** (`Decomp`,
  `Silmaril.Elf.Staged.Decomp.Decomposes`): the symbol-table function extents and explicit gaps tile the
  section exactly. Table: `DECOMP.md`. This is **not** instruction decoding, control flow or semantics.
* **Mapped (tool-derived, not proved)**: each function symbol to its C function (translation unit,
  name, declaration line, signature classes, direct callees), from the DWARF of a debug twin whose code
  is checked byte-identical to the pinned object (`twin.sh`, `funcmap.py`).
* **Frontend run (measured)**: `pp.sh` rebuilds each package with `-save-temps` and keeps its preprocessed
  translation units; `frontend.py` runs the Lean port of the Cerberus frontend (`cerb-lean parse --level tail`)
  on each, results in `<pkg>/frontend/<arch>.tsv`. Most units are rejected inside glibc/gcc system headers
  (GNU extensions); the accepted ones are listed there.
* **Open**: contextual C-to-ELF translation validation. Instantiated statements: 0. Every function has a
  context and its blockers (`TV.md`). No AArch64 ISA semantics exists in silmaril-lean, so no AArch64
  statement can be instantiated.

## Tests (what was run)

All tests run inside the image. x86_64 binaries run natively; aarch64 binaries run under `qemu-aarch64
-L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu`, with `-E LD_LIBRARY_PATH=...` for the shared libraries. Each receipt has
every command and its result.

* **sqlite** -- `sqlite3 :memory:` queries (version, aggregate, built-in sha3, json_object), a file
  database reopened, and `pragma integrity_check`.
* **cjson** -- upstream `test.c` linked against libcjson.so.1, plus our `local/utils_smoke.c` (JSON
  Pointer, RFC 6902 patch generate/apply, RFC 7386 merge patch).
* **jemalloc** -- our `local/je_smoke.c` (mallctl version and arenas.page, 2000 allocations, aligned_alloc,
  realloc, stats). On x86_64 also `LD_PRELOAD` into perl with `MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true`.
* **mimalloc** -- our `local/mi_smoke.c` (mi_version 219; malloc served by mimalloc). On x86_64 also
  `LD_PRELOAD` with `MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1`.
* **darkhttpd** -- serves a directory on 127.0.0.1 and is queried with curl: a text file, a 100 kB
  binary (sha256 compared), a 404, a range request (206) and a directory listing.
* **tcp-pingpong** -- `pingpong-server PORT &` and `pingpong-client 127.0.0.1 PORT 5` in one container.
  Both are native on x86_64 and both run under qemu on aarch64. The transcripts are in the receipts:
  5 x ping/pong.
* **refcrypto** -- our `local/kat.c`: 32/32 known-answer tests pass on both arches. Also the RFC's own
  `shatest.c` against libref_sha2.so: SHA (70 PASSED), HMAC `-m` (35), HKDF `-d` (105), 0 FAILED.
* **coreutils** -- `--version` of all seven, plus true, echo -e, cat -n, wc, head -n, sort, sort -n,
  and sha256sum ("abc" and 10^6 zero bytes).
* **openssl** -- version and `version -f`; dgst sha256, sha3-256 and blake2b512 against standard
  vectors; AES-128 FIPS-197 C.1; an AES-256-CBC/PBKDF2 round trip; Ed25519 genpkey, sign and verify;
  a P-256 self-signed cert; and a TLS 1.3 `s_server -rev` / `s_client` handshake on 127.0.0.1 (both from
  this build; certificate verified; reply reversed).

## Not done / limits

* **GitHub tag/commit archives** (cJSON, mimalloc, darkhttpd, bgnet, XKCP, BLAKE2, poly1305-donna,
  orlp/ed25519) -- These are pinned by sha256. GitHub does not guarantee byte-stable archives; if one
  changes, `fetch.sh` fails loudly rather than build from different bytes.
* **openssl** -- No PGP signature check (sha256 only, which equals the published .sha256). Only
  libcrypto, libssl and the CLI were built; no providers/engines modules and no test suite (`no-tests`).
* **coreutils (aarch64)** -- The cross configure relies on gnulib's conservative guesses. We did not
  supply cache variables to mimic the native results, because none were needed to build. The guesses
  are recorded in `generated/aarch64/configure-cross-guesses.txt`.
* **jemalloc** -- `-funroll-loops` from upstream's configure is kept, so the effective flags are
  `-O2 -funroll-loops`. The aarch64 page size is fixed at 64 KiB (`--with-lg-page=16`).
* **mimalloc** -- Built from the CMake-equivalent gcc command lines, not by CMake itself (CMake is not
  in the image).
* **refcrypto** -- ChaCha20 is DJB's original variant (64-bit nonce, 64-bit counter), not RFC 8439's
  96-bit-nonce interface. The RFC 8439 vectors are still checked where the layouts coincide (first nonce
  word 0). orlp's `ed25519_key_exchange` is in libref_ed25519.so but is not standard X25519 and is not
  tested; standard X25519 comes from libref_x25519.so.
* **aarch64 binaries are larger** -- The aarch64 ELF files are larger than the x86_64 ones mainly because
  of aarch64 ld's 64 KiB segment alignment (max-page-size), not because of more code.
* **Test transcripts** -- Some receipt test records (darkhttpd log lines, random-data sha256) contain
  run-specific values. Only the ELF outputs are covered by the reproducibility check.
